newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Telecom expands to offer Austria networks.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Telecom expands to offer Austria networks.

text.p: Swiss Telecom said it would start offering telecommunication networks for corporate customers in Austria, its latest expansion abroad ahead of liberalisation of its home market next year.

The state group said a new subsidiary based in Vienna, Swisscom Telekom munikations gesellschaft m.b.H., would offer medium and large companies internal networks and connections to global telecoms lines.
At the same time, Swiss Telecom said the Austrian operation aimed to become a leading supplier of "backbone" trunk lines to Internet providers in Austria.

"As customers, the new business is aimed at internationally active companies and other groups with a high demand for communications, especially banks, insurers, industries and state agencies," Swiss Telecom said in a statement.

"The new business with an initial workforce of eight people aims to win over a significant share of larger and medium sized companies in Austria as customers in the next two years," the statement added.

Swiss Telecom is due to be renamed Swisscom in October under plans for a partial privatisation when Switzerland opens its telecommunications market on January 1, 1998, in line with liberalisation in the surrounding European Union.
Swiss law now lets private companies offer some kinds of data transmission but Telecom still controls most voice transmission and the cellular network.
Swiss Telecom expects to lose about 15 percent of its traditional home telephone market to new competitors and expansion abroad is aimed at helping make up for this lost business.

It has invested two billion francs ($1.3 billion) in overseas operations in developing markets -- the Czech Republic, India and Malaysia. It is also a part of Unisource, a joint venture with PTT Telecom of the Netherlands and Telia of Sweden.
Swiss Telecom's net profit last year was down to 746 million Swiss francs from 1995's 1.426 billion after taking restructuring charges of 681 million Swiss francs.
